From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: West Coast lead retreat — travel exception & split-billing routing

Team —

Quick summary: NexaMed is hosting a two-day executive workshop in Redwood City the week of July 12. The account team is requesting a small set of exceptions for our execs and SEs to make the onsite work robust:

- Seat-class upgrade (economy -> premium economy) for three attendees due to back-to-back customer-facing meetings the next day. Estimated incremental cost: $420 total per person.
- Early check-in and late check-out at the contracted hotel for two execs (will require partial hotel upgrade fee).
- Dedicated car service from SFO to Redwood City for one lead (security/guest coordination) instead of rideshare.

Why exceptions: this is a high-touch renewal/expansion opportunity (NX-4567). NexaMed has requested executive presence for the workshop; Alicia (copied) has offered to cost-share for one hotel night per exec under their event support commitment — we need confirmation and a signed MOU.

Action items I'm requesting:
1) Ben/Finance: confirm whether we can route the travel delta to the deal budget (NX-4567) and whether splitting cost with NexaMed is allowed under current procurement rules.
2) Marissa/People: confirm whether the seat upgrade is permissible without VP sign-off for travel policy exceptions.
3) Stephanie/Events: confirm whether our preferred hotel can honor early check-in for the exec block and whether the event manager can attach a line-item invoice separate from room folio.

I've attached a high-level cost_breakdown_kp_v2.xlsx and a draft itinerary. If we get quick alignment this week we can lock flights and avoid higher premiums.

Thanks —

Kimberly Park
Global Head, Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: cost_breakdown_kp_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), itinerary_draft.pdf (pdf stub)

Subject: Re: West Coast lead retreat — travel exception & split-billing routing

Kimberly —

Thanks for the summary. I'm OK with routing incremental travel costs to the deal budget (NX-4567) provided:

- The per-person incremental cost for upgrades stays under $1,000. (From your sheet looks like ~ $420.)
- We have written confirmation from NexaMed that they will cost-share one night per exec (MOU or email).
- We get a pre-authorization on Concur and a PO or charge code to avoid misc expense reconciliation at month-end.

Next steps from my side: I'll open a charge routing request with Finance and mark it as "deal-funded exception". Can you update the cost_breakdown to include a proposed GL code split (50/50 Sales/Marketing) and drop it back to me? If Marissa needs formal VP sign-off after that I'll get it expedited.

Also tagging Alicia — appreciate your help confirming the event support.

-Ben

Ben Carter

On Sat, Jun 20, 2026 at 11:04 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Kimberly —
>
> Thanks for the summary. I'm OK with routing incremental travel costs to the deal budget (NX-4567) provided: ...

Heads-up on policy: travel policy allows seat upgrades only in cases of documented medical need, long-haul flights >6 hours, or with Director+ approval for customer-facing execs. For short West Coast hops we generally deny automatic upgrades.

That said, because this is an executive-level renewal with explicit client request and potential customer-supported cost share, I will approve a one-time exception for premium economy for up to three people provided we have:

1) Written confirmation from NexaMed (email or MOU) that they will cover the one-night hotel support.
2) A documented charge routing entry in Concur with proposed GL codes.
3) Final cost_breakdown.xlsx with per-person line items and expense categories.

I will not sign off on any car service over $150 one-way without Security sign-off due to the executive protection guidelines — if the event manager can confirm an itemized car invoice under $150 we can proceed.

Please create an expense pre-authorization ticket and attach the updated files so Finance can process quickly.

-Marissa

Marissa Cole
Head of People Operations (Travel & Events)
